title: Kitchener’s RISE fund invites applications to support projects that advance equity and wellbeing
content: The City of Kitchener is now accepting applications for the Racialized and Indigenous Supports for Equity (RISE) Fund. The community grant program supports community-led organizations, programs, initiatives and events that help address inequities while increasing opportunities and well-being for Black, Indigenous and racialized communities in Kitchener.

The RISE Fund is open to not-for-profit organizations and community groups in Kitchener, including newly formed groups created for a specific project and established organizations undertaking new initiatives. Eligible organizations must be led by individuals who identify as Black, Indigenous and/or racialized and must support Black, Indigenous and/or racialized communities in Kitchener. Priority is given to newly emerging organizations operating for five years or less, as well as Indigenous groups and organizations.

The fund has an annual budget of $150,000, with grant requests ranging from $1,000 to $10,000 per organization. Funding is available for events, projects and programs that address systemic barriers, increase opportunities for participation and access to resources, and enhance community well-being. Projects and events must take place in Kitchener and demonstrate a clear benefit to local residents.

Applications are being accepted until Monday, September 14 using the City’s online application form. Hard-copy forms and accessibility support are also available, and grant-writing tips are offered on the RISE Fund web page to assist applicants as they prepare their applications.
For eligibility details, application resources and submission information, visit Kitchener.ca/RISE

title: Kitchener’s LoveMyHood matching grant program celebrates neighbourhood leadership
content: The City of Kitchener announced seven new recipients of the 2026 LoveMyHood Matching Grant last evening, bringing the total funding awarded this year to more than $120,000 for resident-led neighbourhood projects.

“LoveMyHood reflects something we've long believed in here in Kitchener, strong neighbourhoods help build a strong city,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “These seven projects will help residents turn great community ideas into action and strengthen neighbourhood connections across Kitchener.”

The approved projects span multiple neighbourhoods and include placemaking, events, neighbourhood art, and greening initiatives led by youth, newcomers, parent councils, neighbourhood associations, and resident groups. Projects are conditionally approved, with city staff working alongside recipients to refine plans and support neighbourhood engagement prior to implementation.

Since launching in 2017, the LoveMyHood grant program has invested more than $1.6 million in over 230 resident-led events, programs, and capital projects in neighbourhoods across Kitchener. Through three intakes, the program awards up to $200,000 annually to support projects that strengthen community connections and community pride.
The third and final grant intake for 2026 is Thursday, October 29.
To learn more about the LoveMyHood Matching Grant, please visit LoveMyHood.ca/LMHgrant .

title: Last day to become a 2026 municipal election candidate is August 21
content: The deadline for candidates interested in running in the 2026 municipal and school board election to file their nomination is Friday, August  21 at 2 p.m.

The City’s website highlights eligibility requirements for who can run for office, elected offices and qualifications, details on filing fees and the nomination process, and helpful resources for becoming a candidate including a candidate's guide and checklist. For more information on how to become a candidate and the nomination process, visit  KitchenerVotes.ca

The City of Kitchener is making it easy for candidates interested in running in the 2026 municipal and school board election to file their nomination documents by offering appointments where staff will review nomination paperwork and share details on the election process.

Appointments can be booked online at KitchenerVotes.ca and will be offered in person at the City’s corporate contact centre. One-hour appointments are available Monday – Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. The last day to book an appointment is Thursday, August  20,  2026. Nominations will be accepted by walk-in only on Friday, Aug ust  21, 2026.
For more information on this year’s election,  visit  KitchenerVotes.ca .
For more information: Corporate Communications and Marketing City of Kitchener media@kitchener.ca

title: Stay active, connect and have fun this fall: City of Kitchener program registration opens August 18 at 8:30 a.m.
content: Officially less than a week away, the City of Kitchener’s fall program registration opens  Tuesday, August 18 at 8:30 a.m. for Kitchener residents (August 25 for non-residents).
Browse hundreds of recreation, sport and leisure opportunities in the Active Kitchener Program Guide .
For older adults, residents aged 55+ can explore programs, activities and social opportunities through the Older Adults Program Guide or by visiting Kitchener.ca/OlderAdults.
Free printed copies are also available at community centres, pools and Kitchener City Hall.
If you're new to Kitchener or registering for the first time, creating your ActiveNet account before August 18 is required to register online for programs.
Before registration opens:
Tip:  Programs saved to your Wish List can be added to your cart quickly once registration opens.
If program fees are preventing you from joining a program, you could qualify for a yearly subsidy of $400 per person in  Leisure Access Fee assistance. Apply before registration day on our website.

If you or a family member requires additional support to participate in a recreation program, Inclusion Support and the Personal Assistance for Leisure (PAL) program can help make participation more accessible and enjoyable.
Register online , in person at community centers, pools or City Hall, or by calling our dedicated registration phone number at 519-741-2907 .

title: KidsPark brings a day of adventure to Victoria Park
content: Get ready to climb, play and explore at  KidsPark, returning to Kitchener this  Sunday, August 16, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. This free, family-friendly festival will transform Victoria Park into a land of adventure packed with live entertainment, hands-on activities, inflatables, games,  crafts and interactive experiences for kids  of all ages.

Families can spend the day exploring themed activity zones throughout the park, including Castle Kingdom, Mighty Machines, Sports Zone, Activity Alley, Dino Island and Pirate Cove, Enchanted Garden, McQueen  Raceway and the KidsPark Market. Visitors can also enjoy train rides on the Heffner Express, meet favourite characters, take in live animal shows and discover activities hosted by more than 75 vendors and community groups.

Live entertainment will take place throughout the day on the Star Stage and Island Stage, featuring performances by  Erick Traplin , a Paw Patrol live show, a Bruno Mars tribute, a sing-along with Moana, Maui, Elsa and Anna, Rumi’s K-pop dance party, pirate shows, dinosaur and animal shows, and a Dino Dance Party.
When  it's time to refuel, families can enjoy a variety of local food trucks serving everything from pizza and bubble tea to sweet treats and picnic favourites.

KidsPark is designed to be welcoming and accessible for all visitors. Accessibility passes will be available for children who require extra support, and families can visit the KPL Calm Corner for a sensory-friendly space to rest and recharge.
The Food Bank of Waterloo Region will also be on-site accepting non-perishable food items or cash donations to help support our community.

KidsPark is easy to reach by transit, bicycle or car. There are many ION and GRT stops within walking distance of the festival grounds. Bike Check will be available with free, secure bike parking by the clocktower. Free vehicle parking is also available at many parking garages and surface lots on Sundays  throughout downtown Kitchener.

The celebration is  happening rain or shine, so p ack a picnic blanket, bring your sense of  adventure and join us for a day filled with music, imagination and unforgettable family memories. Learn more at Kitchener.ca/KidsPark .

title: Joint Statement from the City of Kitchener and Caribana Arts Group Regarding the 2026 Caribana Ignite Festival
content: Recent organizational changes and the time  required to successfully plan and deliver a major cultural festival have made it clear that additional preparation time is needed to ensure the event meets the expectations of the community and participants.

“Caribana Ignite has always been about celebrating Caribbean culture,  community and creativity. While we are disappointed not to move forward in 2026, we believe this pause will allow us to strengthen our organization and build a solid foundation for future success. We remain committed to bringing this celebration back and working alongside our community partners to ensure its long-term success,” said Quammie Williams, Interim Board Chair, Caribana Arts Group .
The City of Kitchener  remains committed to celebrating and supporting Caribbean cultural expression and the rich cultural diversity that helps make Kitchener a vibrant and welcoming community.

Steve Roth, Manager of Special Events,  City of Kitchener, said the  City is disappointed that the festival will not move forward in 2026 but supports the decision to take the time needed to strengthen the City of Kitchener  / Caribana Arts  Group partnership and plan for future success.
"The City of Kitchener values its partnership with Caribana Arts Group and looks forward to continuing conversations and exploring opportunities to welcome this celebration back in the years ahead."
The City of Kitchener and Caribana Arts Group remain committed to ongoing conversations and look forward to exploring possibilities for the 2027 event season and beyond.

title: Encore your summer at Kitchener’s Endless Summer festival, featuring Mother Mother, Valley and more
content: Celebrate the final days of summer at Endless Summer, returning to Victoria Park on Saturday, September 5. This free outdoor festival will bring an all-Canadian lineup of live music, food  trucks and summer fun to the heart of Kitchener from 2 to 11 p.m.

The music starts at 2:30 p.m. with performances from:

title: City of Kitchener announces new full-service restaurant at the Aud
content: The City of Kitchener has selected the Rolleman Restaurant Group, a local owner of several successful restaurants, to operate the new full-service restaurant at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium (The Aud), which will open later this summer.

Following a competitive process that emphasized ‘a vibrant dining experience that celebrates local flavour while complementing The Aud’s high-energy, sports-centric atmosphere’, the Rolleman Restaurant Group was selected to operate the new Club 51 Sports Bar.

In honour of the Aud celebrating its 75 th anniversary this year, the restaurant was named Club 51 to commemorate the year The Aud opened – 1951. With a modern take on the classic sports bar, Club 51 will continue the tradition of bringing community and sport together in one place. The restaurant will open later this summer with a grand opening scheduled for September 18, in time to celebrate the Kitchener Rangers Home Opener.

“We are excited to welcome Club 51 to the Aud and look forward to enjoying the local food, drinks and hospitality they will bring to this incredible new community space,” said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. “Whether hosting fans before a Rangers game, friends watching the game on the big screen, families dining out, or a couple on a date, Club 51 will see community members of all ages joining in to create great times and great memories together.”

Club 51 blends the rich history of this iconic venue with elevated pub fare, local craft beer, Ontario-made beverages and warm hospitality. It will offer a modern and inviting space for up to 120 guests.

“We proudly source from local breweries, producers, and suppliers, celebrating the flavours and businesses of Waterloo Region,” said Jackie Rolleman, co-owner/operator of Club 51. “We will offer the classics like wings, burgers, and nachos with a modern touch, along with menu items highlighting current food trends like protein power bowls and plant-based options.”

With 40 years of combined experience, the Rolleman Restaurant Group operates with a focus on the surrounding community and oversees several locations in Waterloo Region, including Thirteen Food & Beverage in downtown Galt, The Galt Club, The Imperial Restaurant in New Hamburg, and previously, EJ’s at Baden.

“We are excited to create a welcoming place for fans, families, and friends to gather before, during, and after every event,” added Matt Rolleman, co-owner/operator of Club 51. “And not just on game days, but every day.”
In May 2025, Council approved $2M to transform the Subscriber’s Lounge into a 2,300 square foot restaurant offering a vibrant dining experience.

Located on the second floor of The Aud in the newly renovated space, the full-service restaurant will support the Aud’s role as a premier multi-purpose venue and will create opportunities for larger events in the future.
For updates and more information, visit TheAud.ca/Club51 .
